full_judgment:
Kemaluddin Hossain, J.—This appeal by special leave arises out of a judgment and decree passed by a Bench of the High Court of East Pakistan in a First Appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against the defendant-appellants in the suit for damages for breach of contract. 

 2. The plaintiffs A. R. A. G. Limited are respondents: The Plaintiffs are the purchasers, and the defendants, sellers. The plaintiffs contracted to purchase from the defendants, Amin Jute Mills Limited, the appellants before 18. 7. 55, 100 bales of gunny salt bags, each bale containing 400 bags, at the rate of Rs. 85/- per 100 bags inclusive of taxes. Under the contract, the defendants were to ship the goods in August, 1955 at the Karachi address of the plaintiffs, and payment was to be made on production of the bill of lading. The defendants failed to ship the goods and, upon enquiry by the plaintiffs, they were informed that defendants had cancelled the contract by a letter dated 20.7.55. The plaintiffs, denied the receipt of this letter, and imputed breach of contract on the part of defendants. They therefore filed the suit claiming damages, the difference between the contract price and the market price on the due date at the rate of Rs. 15/- per 100 bags amounting to Rs. 6000/-In proof of market price of the goods on due date, namely, 31.8.55, the plaintiffs produced a cash memo Ext. 3 under which they purported to have purchased similar goods in Karachi on 3.9.55 at the rate of Rs. 99/- per bags. The defendants contested the claim on grounds, inter-alia, that the plaintiffs were not entitled to any damages for non-fulfillment of the contract since they suffered no loss on that account. On consideration of evidence the suit was decreed by the trial Court for a sum of Rs. 2,350/- with interest on the basis of the market difference which was calculated between the contract price and the market price at Chittagong on due date at Rs. 76/6 annas. The market price was based on Ext. E, a receipt granted by defendants on 19.8.55 to a firm at Chittagong.The trial Court also took the view that since the difference in price was required to be calculated on the basis of the price prevailing in 31st August, 1955 at Chittagong where the documents of goods were to be delivered, the price shown in Ext. 3 of similar goods at Karachi market could not be taken into consideration. 

 3. The defendants preferred an appeal in the High Court, Dacca and the plaintiffs also filed cross-objection on the ground that the trial Court should have decreed the suit on the basis of the market difference at Karachi. The learned Judges of the High Court dismissed the appeal holding that although the plaintiffs could not prove that they had suffered loss on account of non-delivery of goods, they were entitled under section 73 of the Contract Act, to the difference in price between the date of contract and the due date at the price prevailing at Chittagong market. The cross-objection was dismissed on the ground that the plaintiffs could not specifically prove the amount of loss suffered by them. The defendants only appealed to the Supreme Court.
